Title: Diagnosis of test `isUnixSymlinkIsFalseIfMoreThanOneFlagIsSet`

Details: The test `isUnixSymlinkIsFalseIfMoreThanOneFlagIsSet` opens a ZipFile and retrieves a ZipArchiveEntry for the path "META-INF/maven/". It asserts that the entry is not a Unix symlink by checking `ze.isUnixSymlink()` returns false.

The method `ZipArchiveEntry.isUnixSymlink()` returns true if and only if `(getUnixMode() & UnixStat.LINK_FLAG) == UnixStat.LINK_FLAG`. The `getUnixMode()` method extracts UNIX permission bits from external attributes if the platform is UNIX, otherwise returns 0. Specifically, `getUnixMode()` returns `((getExternalAttributes() >> SHORT_SHIFT) & SHORT_MASK)` when on the UNIX platform.

The `UnixStat.LINK_FLAG` constant is `0120000` (octal), representing the UNIX symbolic link file type bits.

The test expects that if more than one flag is set (e.g. the mode bits include bits beyond the symlink bit), then `isUnixSymlink()` should return false. But the current implementation only checks if the link flag bits are set within the mode, ignoring if other bits are set simultaneously.

Hence, if additional bits besides the symlink bits are set, `(getUnixMode() & LINK_FLAG)` will still equal `LINK_FLAG`, causing `isUnixSymlink()` to return true incorrectly.

This explains the test failure: the implementation incorrectly returns true when multiple file type flags are set, violating the test's expectation that `isUnixSymlink()` must return false in such cases.

Recommended fix: `isUnixSymlink()` should check that the mode bits exactly match the symlink flag, not just include them.

The root cause is this line in `ZipArchiveEntry.isUnixSymlink()`:

```java
return (getUnixMode() & UnixStat.LINK_FLAG) == UnixStat.LINK_FLAG;
```

which should be replaced by:

```java
return getUnixMode() == UnixStat.LINK_FLAG;
```

to ensure only pure symlink file modes return true.

---
